text:
maria: heads up — helm upgrade for gpupool chart (v2.3.1) aborted during post-install hook. Chart was deployed with --atomic, but hook failed and left CRD conversion state inconsistent. :frowning:
ajay: on it. which cluster and region? saw some 502s to the conversion webhook earlier.
maria: eu-west-1-dedicated-gpupool. deploy-bot reported `UPGRADE FAILED` with exit code 1. cloudwatch logs show repeated 504s from conversion webhook.
carla: can you paste the hook failure snippet? also any drift from gitops? Argo hasn't reconciled yet AFAIK.
maria: snippet:
```
post-install hook gpupool-migrate failed: conversion webhook returned 504: context deadline exceeded
operator-controller: failed to update CRD status, requeue
```
ajay: that's the same pattern we saw when two CRD conversions ran in parallel and the API server queued one. Should we pause further rollouts? If conversion gets stuck it blocks operators.
maria: paused the rollout in the pipeline and put a hold in the PR. notif sent to oncall. :hand:
sre-oncall: I'm watching. If this stays >10m I'll open an incident. Any risk to running workloads (inference pods)?
tim: inference pods are fine — gpupool operator wasn't upgraded so existing pods continue. risk is operator stuck reconciling new CRs; not immediate eviction.
carla: FYI there was a related terraform change that adjusted the gpupool CRD schema last week — possible race with the helm chart which includes a CRD bundle. We should avoid applying schema changes and CRD upgrades at same time as controller upgrades.
ajay: quick mitigation until we fix the hook: remove the failed hook resources and force the operator back to previous release. Steps I propose:
1) kubectl delete job -n redwood gpupool-postinstall-xxxxx  # remove dangling hook job
2) helm rollback redwood-gpupool 1 --namespace redwood
3) if CRD conversion remains stuck, patch the CRD to remove stale conversion status:
```
kubectl patch crd gpupools.redwood.ai -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood/conversion-hint":"clear"}}}' --type=merge
```
(note: this is a temporary manual fix)
maria: tried deleting the hook job but CRD status still shows conversion in progress. rollback succeeded but helm still reports "previous release in failed state" in CI.
deploy-bot: automatic rollback executed for release redwood-gpupool (revision 1). CI check: helm status shows FAILED -> ROLLED BACK.
carla: ok good. follow-up: add a pre-upgrade hook to the chart that checks CRD conversion readiness before attempting post-install migrations. Also guard the terraform CRD changes behind a deployment window.
tim: I'll open a tiny PR to add a readiness hook (simple `kubectl get crd gpupools.redwood.ai -ojsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'` check with retries). Put canary to 10% of dedicated clusters first.
ajay: also let's add a GitOps preflight: argocd/flux should detect CRD schema diffs and block auto-sync if operator version changes at same time. We saw env drift: the TF change updated schema in staging earlier but didn't in prod.
sre-oncall: noted. creating short runbook entry for this exact failure mode: "helm atomic upgrade leaves CRD in conversion state" and escalation steps. tagging @platform-oncall.
maria: cost/capacity note — while we recover, avoid force-scaling nodes in ap-south-1 or ap-southeast; GPU capacity is tight there (p4d quotas). If operator restarts and triggers a rebalance it could spike spot gets and cost.
carla: +1. We'll coordinate any scale-ups through capacity team. For now keep operator replicas at current count and avoid rolling node pools.
ajay: post-mortem items: 1) add pre-upgrade CRD readiness hook 2) avoid simultaneous TF CRD schema changes + chart upgrades 3) GitOps preflight block 4) automatic retry/backoff for conversion webhook calls in operator.
tim: opening PRs and the runbook now. tagging owners in PR descriptions. anyone want to take the rollback retro?
maria: I'll write a short incident blurb and link the PRs. thanks all. :thumbsup:
